summary: Breidoun Aviation Holdings, Inc. (Buyer, the firm's client) bought all outstanding stock of Ostrander Skyline Catering, Inc. from Miriv Provisioning Group, LLC (Seller). Ostrander is a regional airline caterer that runs commissaries supplying inflight meals, galley provisioning and crew meals to regional carriers. Closing took place on July 1, 2026. Seller then signed a Confirmatory IP Assignment Agreement dated September 25, 2026, transferring recipes, menu specifications and the brand to Ostrander, with a Buyer joinder. That agreement selects Delaware law and Delaware forums. Under the SPA's precedence clause it controls as to its subject matter, and through that clause it pulls Seller's IP-representation liability under the SPA indemnity cap. The recitals of the IP Assignment Agreement also record the post-closing price dispute. Seller delivered its Closing Statement on August 3, 2026. Buyer delivered its Notice of Disagreement on September 18, 2026, outside the 30-day window in the SPA. Seller rejects the notice as untimely and Buyer reserves its position. The Key Employee Agreement with Ostrander's executive chef and general manager defines "Business" more narrowly than the SPA, so her non-compete leaves galley provisioning and crew meal services open to her. A linen and galley-cart washing services agreement is in the folder as a distractor.

issues.label: IP Assignment selects Delaware law and forum, contrary to SPA
issues.description: SPA Section 11.8 (D1) selects New York law. It also makes New York County courts the exclusive forum for disputes under any Transaction Document. Section 10 of the Confirmatory IP Assignment Agreement (D2) selects the laws of the State of Delaware and the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware Court of Chancery. SPA Section 11.10 (D1) provides that an Ancillary Agreement controls as to its subject matter, so the SPA's choice does not cure the conflict. As a result, disputes over title to the transferred recipes, menu specifications and brand, which are the core assets of the target, go to Delaware under Delaware law. Indemnity claims under the SPA for the same facts go to New York under New York law. Breidoun faces split proceedings, inconsistent results and higher cost. The rule that the SPA controls does not apply here because of the subject-matter exception in Section 11.10.
detect_terms: laws of the State of Delaware
Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware
issues.expected_finding: The IP Assignment's Delaware law and exclusive Delaware Chancery forum control over IP matters under SPA Section 11.10, conflicting with the SPA's New York law and exclusive New York County forum in Section 11.8. Breidoun therefore risks parallel proceedings in two forums over the same IP facts, so the IP Assignment should be amended to adopt New York law and New York County courts, or the precedence clause should be carved back for governing law and forum.

issues.label: Key Employee non-compete uses a narrower "Business"
issues.description: SPA Section 1.1 (D1) defines "Business" as inflight catering, galley provisioning and crew meal services for regional air carriers. SPA Section 6.9 (D1) requires Seller to cause the Key Employee to sign a non-compete covering the Business. The Key Employee Agreement (D3) defines "Business" in Section 1 as only the preparation of hot inflight meals for regional air carriers. Its non-compete in Section 7 restricts only that "Business". Under SPA Section 11.10, the Key Employee Agreement controls as to its own subject matter. Read together, these provisions mean the departing executive chef and GM may lawfully compete in galley provisioning and crew meal services, two of the three acquired service lines, using knowledge of Ostrander's customers.
issues.expected_finding: The Key Employee Agreement's definition of "Business" covers only hot inflight meal preparation, while the SPA's definition also covers galley provisioning and crew meal services, so Solvig's non-compete leaves those lines unprotected. Breidoun should require an amendment that conforms the definition to SPA Section 1.1 and should consider a claim against Seller under SPA Section 6.9.

issues.label: Notice of Disagreement delivered after 30-day window
issues.description: SPA Section 2.4(b) (D1) gives Buyer 30 days after delivery of the Closing Statement to deliver a Notice of Disagreement. If Buyer does not deliver one in time, the Closing Statement becomes final and binding. Recital C of the Confirmatory IP Assignment Agreement (D2) records that Seller delivered the Closing Statement on August 3, 2026, so the window closed on September 2, 2026. Recital D (D2) records that Breidoun delivered its Notice of Disagreement on September 18, 2026, 16 days late. The same recital records that Seller rejects the notice as untimely and that Breidoun expressly reserves its position. Breidoun has not accepted the Closing Statement, so the matter remains open, but the purchase price adjustment is at serious risk of being fixed at Seller's figures.
detect_terms: within 30 days after delivery of the Closing Statement
issues.expected_finding: Under SPA Section 2.4(b), Breidoun's window to dispute the Closing Statement delivered August 3, 2026 expired September 2, 2026, so its September 18, 2026 Notice of Disagreement is late and the Closing Statement may be deemed final and binding. Because Breidoun has reserved its position in Recital D of the IP Assignment Agreement, it should promptly seek a written extension or tolling from Seller and assess any defects in Seller's delivery to preserve the dispute.

issues.label: IP Assignment pulls IP rep breaches under the SPA cap
issues.description: SPA Section 9.5(a) (D1) caps Seller's indemnity at 10% of the Purchase Price. SPA Section 9.5(b) (D1) excludes Fraud, Fundamental Representations and breaches of Section 4.12 (Intellectual Property) from that cap. Section 8.3 of the later Confirmatory IP Assignment Agreement (D2) provides that Seller's liability for breach of that agreement or of the representations in SPA Section 4.12 is subject to the cap in SPA Section 9.5(a), and it does so notwithstanding Section 9.5(b). Because SPA Section 11.10 (D1) gives the Ancillary Agreement control as to its subject matter, the IP-specific provision displaces the carve-out. Losses from defective title to recipes, menu specifications or the brand are therefore now capped at 10% of the Purchase Price instead of being uncapped.
detect_terms: subject to the Cap set forth in Section 9.5(a)
issues.expected_finding: IP Assignment Section 8.3, which controls over IP matters under SPA Section 11.10, removes the SPA Section 9.5(b) carve-out for breaches of the Section 4.12 IP representations, so Breidoun's recovery for IP title defects is now limited to 10% of the Purchase Price. Section 8.3 should be deleted or amended to preserve the uncapped carve-out.
